questions.q: In a double slit experiment shown in figure, when light of wavelength 400 nm is used, dark fringe is observed at P. If D=0.2 m, the minimum distance between the slits S1 and S2 is α mm. Write the value of 10α to the nearest integer.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to the given diagram, the path difference for minima at P is given by

∆x=2D2+d2-2D   ...1

And, from the condition of minima, it follows that

∆x=λ2   ...2

Equations (1) and (2) imply that

2D2+d2-2D=λ2

⇒D2+d2-D=λ4

⇒D2+d2=λ4+D

⇒D2+d2=D2+λ216+Dλ2

⇒d2=Dλ2+λ216

⇒d2=0.2×400×10-92+16×10-1416

⇒d2≈400×10-10

∴d=20×10-5 m=0.20 mm

Therefore, 10α=2.

questions.q: Sodium light of wavelengths <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>650</mn><mo> </mo><mi>nm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>655</mn><mo> </mo><mi>nm</mi></math> is used to study diffraction at a single slit of aperture <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>. The distance between the slit and the screen is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The separation between the positions of the first maxima of diffraction pattern obtained in the two cases is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The condition for maxima in diffraction is,

bsinθ=2n+1λ2.

 For the first maxima n=1. Therefore,

bsinθ=3λ2⇒sinθ=3λ2b=yDy=3λD2b

Now the difference between the positions of the maxima will be,

y1-y2=3D2bλ1-λ2⇒y1-y2=3×22×5×10-4×655-650×10-9=3×10-5 m

questions.q: A source of light is placed in front of a screen. The intensity of light on the screen is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>I</mi></math>. Two Polaroids <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> are so placed in between the source of light and screen that the intensity of light on the screen is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>I</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>. Then the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>, should be rotated by an angle of (degrees) so that the intensity of light on the screen becomes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>I</mi></mrow><mn>8</mn></mfrac></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Recall the law of Malus I'=I2cos2θ

Here θ is the angle between two polaroids, 

⇒3I8=I2cos2θ⇒θ=30°.

questions.q: In Young’s double slit experiment, two slits S1 and S2 are d distance apart and the separation from slits to screen is D (as shown in figure). Now if two transparent slabs of equal thickness 0.1 mm but refractive index 1.51 and 1.55 are introduced in the path of beam λ=4000 Å from S1 and S2 respectively. The central bright fringe spot will shift by ________ number of fringes.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The change in path difference due to the two slabs at P is Δx=μ2-μ1t

=(1.55-1.51)×0.1=0.04×10-4

⇒Δx=4×10-6=4 μm

Now, the distance of central maxima from geometrical center is y=ΔxDd=4×10-6Dd

Now, fringe width, nβ=4×10-6 Dd

Or, nλDd=4×10-6 Dd

Number of shift, n=4×10-64×10-7=10.

questions.q: In a single slit diffraction pattern, a light of wavelength <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6000</mn><mo> </mo><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mover></math> is used. The distance between the first and third minima in the diffraction pattern is found to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> when the screen is placed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> away from slits. The width of the slit is ____<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For nth minima:

⇒bsinθ=nλ

(λ is very small, so sinθ is very small, hence sinθ≃tanθ.

⇒btanθ=nλ

⇒byD=nλ

⇒yn=nλDb (Position of nth minima)

B→1st  minima and A→3rd :

y3=3λDb,y1=λDb

⇒Δy=y3-y1=2λDb

⇒3×10-3=2×6000×10-10×0.5b

⇒b=2×6000×10-10×0.53×10-3

⇒b=2×10-4 m

questions.q: An unpolarized light beam is incident on the polarizer of a polarization experiment and the intensity of light beam emerging from the analyzer is measured as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn></math> Lumens. Now, if the analyzer is rotated around the horizontal axis (direction of light) by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo></math> in clockwise direction, the intensity of emerging light will be _______Lumens.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Assuming initially axis of Polarizer and Analyzer are parallel

Now emerging intensity =I02cos230°

=100322=100×34=75

questions.q: A Young's double-slit experiment is performed using monochromatic light of wavelength <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">λ</mi></math>. The intensity of light at a point on the screen, where the path difference is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">λ</mi></math>, is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> units. The intensity of light at a point where the path difference is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">λ</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></math> is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>nK</mi><mn>12</mn></mfrac></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></math> is an integer. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></math> is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
I=I0cos2ϕ2

=kcos2πλ×λ6

=k cos2π6

=3k4=9k12

n=9

questions.q: A parallel beam of monochromatic light of wavelength <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5000</mn><mo> </mo><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mover></math> is incident normally on a single narrow slit of width <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>001</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>. The light is focused by convex lens on screen, placed on its focal plane. The first minima will be formed for the angle of diffraction of ______ (degree).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The condition for the first minima in the single slit diffraction experiment can be written as

asinθ=λ   ...1

Equation (1) implies that

sinθ=λa=5000×10-101×10-6=12

⇒θ=30°

questions.q: In a Young's double slit experiment <math><mn>15</mn></math> fringes are observed on a small portion of the screen when light of wavelength <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>500</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> is used. Ten fringes are observed on the same section of the screen when another light source of wavelength <math><mi>λ</mi></math> is used. Then the value of <math><mi>λ</mi></math> is (in <math><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> ) __________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
15×500×Dd=10×λ2×Dd
λ2=15×50 nm
λ2=750 nm

questions.q: White light is passed through a double slit and interference is observed on a screen <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> away. The separation between the slits is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>. The first violet and red fringes are formed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> away from the central white fringes. The difference in wavelengths of red and violet light is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mtext>in</mtext><mo> </mo><mi>nm</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>.</mo></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
y1=λrDd

y2=λvDd

λr−λv=y1−y2dD=(3.5−2)mm×0.3mm1.5m=300nm

questions.q: Two wavelengths $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ are used in Young's double slit experiment. $\lambda_1=450 \mathrm{~nm}$ and $\lambda_2=650 \mathrm{~nm}$. The minimum order of fringe produced by $\lambda_2$ which overlaps with the fringe produced by $\lambda_1$ is $n$. The value of $n$ is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{n}_2 \lambda_2=\mathrm{n}_1 \lambda_1 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{n}_2}{\mathrm{n}_1}=\frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2}=\frac{450}{650}=\frac{9}{13} \\ & \mathrm{n}_2=9\end{aligned}$

questions.q: In a Young's double slit experiment, two slits are located 1.5 mm apart. The distance of screen from slits is 2 m and the wavelength of the source is 400 nm. If the 20 maxima of the double slit pattern are contained within the centre maximum of the single slit diffraction pattern, then the width of each slit is $\mathrm{x} \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~cm}$, where x -value is ________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Width of 20 maxima of double slit $=$ width of central maxima of single slit
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{20 \lambda \mathrm{D}}{\mathrm{~d}}=\frac{2 \lambda \mathrm{D}}{\mathrm{a}} \\ & \frac{10}{\mathrm{~d}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{a}} \\ & \mathrm{a}=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{10}=\frac{1.5 \times 10^{-1}}{10} \mathrm{~cm}=15 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~cm}
\end{aligned}$
Value of $x$ is 15
Answer is 15

questions.q: As shown in the figure, in Young's double slit experiment, a thin plate of thickness t=10 μm and refractive index μ=1.2 is inserted infront of slit S1. The experiment is conducted in air (μ=1) and uses a monochromatic light of wavelength λ=500 nm. Due to the insertion of the plate, central maxima is shifted by a distance of xβ0. β0 is the fringe-width before the insertion of the plate. The value of the x is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Fringe shift due to slab in Young's double slit experiment is given by ∆x=D(μ-1)td

Since, fringe width β0=Ddλ

Then, ∆x=β0μ-1tλ

Putting the values, we have

=10×10-6(1.2-1)5×10-7 β0

=10-5×0.25×10-7β0=4β0

Hence, the value of x=4.

questions.q: In a Young’s double slit experiment, the intensities at two points, for the path difference <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>λ</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>λ</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math> (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>λ</mi></math> being the wavelength of light used) are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> respectively. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math> denotes the intensity produced by each one of the individual slits, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know, resultant intensity is given by,

I=4I0 cos2Δϕ2 and phase difference can be written as ∆ϕ=2πλ∆x.

For first case:

I1=4I0 cos22πλ×λ4=4I0 cos2π4=2I0

For second case:

I2=4I0 cos22πλ×λ3=4I0 cos22π3=I0

Therefore, required value ofI1+I2I0=3.

questions.q: In a Young's double slit experiment, a laser light of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>560</mn><mo> </mo><mi>nm</mi></math> produces an interference pattern with consecutive bright fringes' separation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>7</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>. Now another light is used to produce an interference pattern with consecutive bright fringes' separation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>. The wavelength of second light is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>nm</mi><mo>.</mo></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here: λ1=560×10-9 m, β1=7.2×10-3 m and β2=8.1×10-3 m.

Let d be the width and D be the distance between slit and screen then fringe width, β=λDd.

Thus, from above, β∝λ

So, the wavelength of second light is λ2=β2β1λ1=98λ1

∴   λ2=98×560=630 nm.

questions.q: The width of one of the two slits in a Young's double slit experiment is three times the other slit. If the amplitude of the light coming from a slit is proportional to the slit-width, the ratio of minimum to maximum intensity in the interference pattern is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>:</mo><mo> </mo><mn>4</mn></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mo>.</mo></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given amplitude $\propto$ slit width
Also intensity $\propto(\text { Amplitude })^2 \propto(\text { Slit width })^2$
$\frac{I_1}{I_2}=\left(\frac{3}{1}\right)^2=9 \Rightarrow I_1=9 I_2$
$\frac{I_{\min }}{I_{\max }}=\left(\frac{\sqrt{I_1}-\sqrt{I_2}}{\sqrt{I_1}+\sqrt{I_2}}\right)^2=\left(\frac{3-1}{3+1}\right)^2=\frac{1}{4}=\frac{x}{4}$
$\Rightarrow x=1$

questions.q:
In a Young's double slit experiment, the intensity at a point is $\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^{\text {th }}$ of the maximum intensity, the minimum distance of the point from the central maximum is ________ $\mu \mathrm{m}$. 
(Given : $\lambda=600 \mathrm{~nm}, \mathrm{~d}=1.0 \mathrm{~mm}, \mathrm{D}=1.0 \mathrm{~m}$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{I}=\mathrm{I}_0 \cos ^2\left(\frac{\Delta \phi}{2}\right) \\ & \frac{\mathrm{I}_0}{4}=\cos ^2\left(\frac{\Delta \phi}{2}\right) \\ & \Delta \phi=\frac{2 \pi}{3} \\ & \frac{2 \pi}{\lambda}\left(\frac{\mathrm{yd}}{\mathrm{D}}\right)=\frac{2 \pi}{3} \\ & \mathrm{y}=\frac{\lambda \mathrm{D}}{3 \mathrm{~d}}=\frac{600 \times 10^{-9} \times 1}{3 \times 10^{-3}}=2 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A double slit interference experiment performed with a light of wavelength 600 nm forms an interference fringe pattern on a screen with 10 th bright fringe having its centre at a distance of 10 mm from the central maximum. Distance of the centre of the same 10th bright fringe from the central maximum when the source of light is replaced by another source of wavelength 660 nm would be _________ mm .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Position of the $n^{\text {th }}$ bright fringe w.r.t. central maxima
in a YDSE is $y_n=n \frac{\lambda D}{d}$.
$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{y_{10}^{\prime}}{y_{10}}=\frac{\lambda^{\prime}}{\lambda}$
or $\quad y_{10}^{\prime}=\frac{\lambda^{\prime}}{\lambda} y_{10}\begin{aligned} & =\left(\frac{660 \mathrm{~nm}}{600 \mathrm{~nm}}\right) 10 \mathrm{~mm} \\ & =11 \mathrm{~mm}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A fringe width of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> was produced for two slits separated by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> apart. The screen is placed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> away. The wavelength of light used is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>nm</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> to the nearest integer is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
β=λDd

λ=βdD

λ=6×10-3×10-310

λ=6×10-7 m=600×10-9 m

λ=600 nm

questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment the two slits are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> distance apart. Interference pattern is observed on a screen at a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>80</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from the slits. The first dark fringe is observed on the screen directly opposite to one of the slits. The wavelength of light will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>nm</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to the question, the first dark fringe is observed directly opposite to one of the slits. Therefore, half of the fringe width is equal to half of the distance between the slits.

β2=d2⇒β=d=6 mm

⇒λDd=0.6×10-3⇒ λ=0.6×10-3dD⇒ λ=0.6×10-3×0.6×10-380×10-2

⇒λ=450×10-9 m=450 nm
